verdict.falsifier: _score's z-scoring puts b on the scale section 3.5 item 1 claims: b_max = 1.0 really is one standard deviation of psi_hat as the policy actually sees it.
verdict.detail: At the only n_live a decision ever occurs at -- n_live = M = 40, because policy_loop.py:145 consults the policy only when the row's memory is full, and the measured min n_live over real evictions is M -- the per-step normalizer is 0.98038 +/- 0.01012 of psi_hat's true sd, against a normal-theory prediction of 0.98111. So b_max = 1.0 is 0.9804 true sd, i.e. item 1's claim is off by 2.0%, and switching to unbiased=True changes 0.0042 of victims at gamma_b = 0.05. The brief's predicted failure is real only in the fill period, where the ratio falls to 0.5641 +/- 0.0055 at n_live = 2 -- and no eviction ever happens there, so it is never exercised. The per-step/pooled ratio IS systematically < 1 (0.93260 +/- 0.00665), but essentially all of that gap is between-step drift in the per-step MEAN, an additive constant shared by every live slot that cannot move an argmin; replacing the per-step sd with a fixed pooled normalizer changes 0.0579 of victims at gamma_b = 0.05. Correction 4's gamma_b range was therefore derived against the right denominator, and cycle 2's 56-60% takeover is not a normalizer artifact: b_max = 1.0 is 3.248 +/- 0.045 times the MEDIAN top-2 z-margin at n_live = 40, which is an order-statistics property of 40 samples. phi is UNTRAINED; uniform weight-scale drift is exactly invariant and rank-1 drift moves nothing either, because psi_hat is a linear functional of s for any phi of this form -- only the GESTALT DISTRIBUTION can move the calibration.
